title: Operator geo-safeguard: KMS binding gate + audit fanout
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Customers running private deployments have asked for a lightweight operator-level guard that prevents accidental cross-region KMS usage for operator-initiated actions (deploys, migrations, emergency keys) while improving audit granularity for residency-sensitive requests. This PR implements an operator geo-safeguard: a decision-time KMS binding gate that enforces operator locality constraints and an audit fanout path that stamps and forwards residency evidence to the audit pipeline.

Goals: 1) Reject operator-scoped KMS operations that violate configured geo-policies; 2) Emit compact residency evidence and immutable audit headers for downstream compliance systems; 3) Provide an opt-in shadow mode and safe rollout path for Dedicated/Private installs.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): - [x] Add operator KMS binding evaluation middleware; - [x] Emit residency_evidence header and signed audit envelope for operator events; - [x] Shadow-rollout flag and CLI toggle; - [x] Unit + integration tests for decision paths; - [x] Docs updates (runbook + config examples); - [x] Telemetry (decision counters, rejection metrics).

Why this is different: Existing residency enforcement lives at request-level in the ingress. Operator actions are often initiated from the control-plane and use separate credentials; they historically bypass certain residency checks. This PR closes that gap by introducing a compact evaluation layer inside the operator service and re-using the policy decision engine (RBACv2 adapter) with operator-scoped constraints. It also fans out a signed audit envelope to the audit collector so compliance consumers can reconcile operator actions with tenant residency claims.

Rolling plan: feature flag "operator_geo_safeguard" defaults to shadow mode. After 2 weeks of shadow metrics and no false positives in staging, flip to enforce in Dedicated/private customer channels.

review_comments: Diego Marquez (2026-01-12): Can we clarify how operator credentials are distinguished from user requests in the policy adapter? I see a tenancy claim is used but we should ensure there is no Privilege Escalation path.
Asha Rao (2026-01-13): The signed envelope payload is large — did we consider compressing the evidence or sending a reference blob? Could be important for high-throughput operator events.
Evan Chen (2026-01-14): Integration tests are great. I hit a flaky test on the CI run related to timing of the fanout retries — marking as a required followup to stabilize.
Security SME (2026-01-15): Suggest adding an MTLs guard when contacting external KMS providers in Private installs. Also ensure HSM/KMS provenance is included in the envelope.
Compliance (2026-01-16): Requesting example policy configs for EU vs non-EU tenants in the docs before enabling enforce mode for customers.

Maya Patel (2026-01-14): Evan — increased retry backoff and added jitter to integration harness; CI flaky test re-ran and passed on second attempt. Marked stabilization ticket ENG-4890.
Maya Patel (2026-01-15): Security SME — added optional mTLS enforcement config and included kms_provenance in the signed envelope. See infra/config/operator_geo_safeguard.yaml.
